name: MAISON MAYLE
band_note: mean of blouse and sweater entry $375 (women's price pass, 2026-10-13)
why: Women's blouses, dresses, knitwear, trousers, shoes and jewelry, mostly $400–$850, sold through its own site and a New York shop.
origin: Founded in New York, United States in 1999 by Jane Mayle.

quote.q: From its inception, Mayle established itself as a brand where slim, chic basics meet vintage inspired pieces that can be easily layered, lived in, and loved.

opview: “From its inception, Mayle established itself as a brand where slim, chic basics meet vintage inspired pieces that can be easily layered, lived in, and loved.” — Maison Mayle (house), About, maisonmayle.com

facts_read.source: brand site (about, Fall Moves collection, lookbook pages, store, terms); Vinted catalogue + item page; TRR designer index (2026-10-13 list); B Lab directory; GOTS database

doors.note: US: 1 own door, 'the shop at 33 Great Jones Street', New York — open Tuesday–Friday 12–6pm, other times by appointment. No other store on the site. New York label (Jane Mayle).

craft_evidence.owned: no evidence — own NoLita boutique since 1999; no workroom named
craft_evidence.mills: no — cloth origins given ('Italian cotton', 'imported Japanese cotton', 'Italian lambskin'), no mill
craft_evidence.madein: ~78% (62 of 80 sampled styles say 'Made in New York' / 'Made in NYC')
craft_evidence.heritage: dated and placed — label founded Fall 1999 with a NoLita boutique; designer Jane Mayle (born London); paused 2009–2015
craft_evidence.reasoning: About four in five product pages say 'Made in New York', and the founding is dated and placed (NoLita, 1999), but no workroom, factory or mill is named. A city of making stated across most of the range, with nothing behind it, is a 2.
